contexts.text: And I will drink () = the instruction of truth thence. To drink = to be instructed. Where the goods and truths of faith are treated of in the Word, to drink = to be instructed in them, and to receive them. Illustrated.
To drink = to perceive. In the internal sense, to drink also = to be communicated and conjoined, and is predicated of what is spiritual, as to eat is predicated of what is celestial. References.

When the camels had made an end of drinking () = acknowledgement from enlightenment in general scientifics... To drink, here, = the same as to draw waters, and also as to drink, above; namely, to be enlightened.
A state of vastated truth is signified by they shall drink water according to measure ().

They did eat and drink () = the appropriation of good and truth thus initiated... To drink (as well as to eat) = to be communicated and conjoined, thus to be appropriated; but as it is predicated of wine, and wine = truth, it is the appropriation of truth which is signified by to drink. AC 3333. AC 3513:2. AC 5120.
They did eat and drink () = communication... To drink = to be communicated as to those things which are of truth. References.
He brought him wine, and he drank () = the conjunction of truth afterwards.
To come to drink () = the affection of truth... because it involves thirst.
Eating and drinking () = their state as to the appropriation of evil and falsity... To drink = the appropriation of truth; thus, in the opposite, the appropriation of falsity.

I will not drink from now of this product of the vine, until that day when I shall drink it new with you in My Father's Kingdom (): the good from truth and the truth from good, by means of which the Intellectual becomes new, or man becomes spiritual, is signified by the product of the vine; its appropriation is signified by to drink... and that this will not take place fully except in the other life, is signified by, until the day when I shall drink it new with you in My Father's Kingdom.

He wanted to give me something to drink. There was in it such a [power] from phantasy, that it would take away understanding from those who drank it. This was represented, because he had deprived of the understanding of truth and good those who had adhered to him in the world.

And they drank () = the application of truths under good. To drink = the communication and appropriation of truth; hence, also, its application. The reason it is under good, is that all the application of truth takes place under good.
And they drank plentifully () = abundantly. To drink = to apply truths under good.

The Egyptians shall labour to drink the waters from the river () = that they would be willing to know scarcely anything concerning it... To drink = to be instructed in truths; hence, to labour to drink = not to be willing to be instructed...

All the Egyptians dug about the river for waters to drink () = search for truth which they might apply to falsities... To drink = to apply to falsities. To drink = to apply, for he who drinks, applies to himself...
Because they could not drink from the waters of the river () = no application from mere falsities... To drink = to apply.

They could not drink the waters for bitterness, because they were bitter () = that truths appeared undelightful to them, because they were devoid of the affection of good. To drink waters = to receive truths, and apply them under good.

Saying, What shall we drink? () = that they could not endure truths because they were undelightful from no affection for them. To drink = to be instructed in truths, and to receive them, also to be affected with them, and thence to appropriate them. References.

There was no water for the people to drink () = the lack of truth, and thence of refreshment... To drink = to be instructed in the truths of faith, and to receive them; here, to be refreshed; for as water and drink refresh the natural life, so do truths and the Knowledges of truth refresh the spiritual life; for he who is in spiritual life, longs to be supported by such things as are called heavenly meats and drinks, which are the goods and truths of faith...
If anyone thirst, let him come unto Me, and drink ()... To drink = to be instructed.

And the people shall drink () = (truths of faith) which will refresh them, and will give them spiritual life. To drink = to be instructed in the truths of faith, and thus to give and refresh spiritual life. AC 9050:12.
To tread the must, but not to drink the wine () = to be instructed concerning the truths which are from good, but still not to appropriate them.

They ate and drank () = information concerning the good and truth of worship... To drink = the conjunction and appropriation of truth. References... The reason it also = information concerning truth, is that... spiritual drink is all the truth of faith from which comes intelligence. References.
To drink spiritually is to be instructed in truths, and, in the opposite sense, in falsities; thus to imbibe them. References.
To drink () = the appropriation of falsity. AC 10466.
(Moses) drank no water () = meanwhile no appropriation of the truth of faith... To drink = the reception and appropriation of truth.
To drink blood () = to appropriate Divine truth from the Word.
He shall drink of the wine of the anger of God () = to imbue the life with the goods and truths of the Word falsified... To drink = to appropriate them, or to imbue the life with them.

Thou hast given them blood to drink, for they are worthy () = that... it was permitted those who have confirmed themselves in faith alone in doctrine and in life to falsify the truths of the Word, and to imbue their life with them so falsified. To drink blood = not only to falsify the truths of the Word, but also to imbue the life with them so falsified; for he who drinks, appropriates to himself and imbues.
Under Pleasure, see this reference.
Such as had indulged in drinking...
He could give to drink out of various cups, and thus cause them to comprehend as he said; for to drink is to instruct and persuade.
Under Dog, see this reference.
She poured out something... like a liquor to drink... They drank of it, and then they... began to rave.
A Christian lives in the outward form like anybody else... he can eat and drink well, but not make his life consist in these things, or take delight in superabundance, and also not in drunkenness.
Under Eat, see these references. AE 840:5.
To drink and be drunken () = to imbibe falsities and commingle them with truths, and thence to be insane. AE 6.
Under Drunk, see these references. AE 329:10. AE 617:24.
To drink the Lord's blood = to receive that truth, to appropriate it, and thus be conjoined with the Lord.
To drink () = to consume... Worship thence is signified by to praise Jehovah and to drink in the courts of holiness.
Not to drink () = the deprivation of truth.
To eat up and drink () = goods and truths to be communicated and appropriated.
To come to the Lord and drink = to receive from Him the truths of doctrine and their faith. AE 622:4.
To drink from the stream () = to learn something thence.

To eat and drink, in the Word, = to eat and drink spiritually, which is to be instructed, and by instruction and life to imbue and appropriate good and truth, thus intelligence and wisdom. Illustrated.
To drink () = to learn and receive.
We drink our waters for silver () = instruction from ourselves, whence come mere falsities.
Drink ye all of it... To drink = to receive, to appropriate, and thus to be conjoined.
A thirsty one as it were drinketh while he dreameth () = an erroneous opinion and faith as of truth.
Be not solicitous... as to what ye shall drink... To drink = intellectually, thus spiritually, to perceive truth.
They drank () = the imbuing of falsity.
He shall drink of the wine of the anger of God = the appropriation of falsity and thence of evil... To drink = to imbue and appropriate.
To drink of the cup of which the Lord drinks () = to undergo temptations.
To drink () = to appropriate to themselves.
Thou hast given them blood to drink = that thence they are in the falsities of evil. To drink blood = to imbibe falsities.
